guide_line: Predict a precipitate and write the net ionic equation.
steps: Nitrate and Group 1 salts dissolve. Chloride dissolves except AgCl, PbCl2, and Hg2Cl2.
Sulfate dissolves except BaSO4, PbSO4, and SrSO4. Carbonate does not, unless it is Group 1 or ammonium.
Swap the ion partners. A solid stays together in the net ionic equation.
Spectator ions appear the same on both sides. Leave them out.
Type yes or no for solubility. For a net ionic equation, use symbols and a hyphen for the charge.
Chlorides dissolve, with a short exception list.

similar_problem.q: Net ionic equation for AgNO3(aq) + NaCl(aq)?
similar_problem.hint: AgCl is the solid. Na+ and NO3- stay in solution.
